messages:
Alex W: Heads up — since the key rotation yesterday our on-prem SCIM webhook is intermittently creating users without roles, or sometimes assigning the wrong role (admin vs engineer). Seeing it across 3 tenants. :rotating_light:
Priya S: Ugh. Any logs? first guess is KMS context/key mismatch after rotation.
Samir K: Can you paste the scim-handler error? also which deployment (VPC or air-gapped onprem)?
Alex W: Private onprem (customer-managed KMS + HSM). Here's the most common error from the handler:
```
2026-03-19T22:14:02Z scim-handler ERROR KMS decrypt failed: Verification failed, context mismatch (expected: \"scim-v1:org-123\", got: \"scim:org-123\") request_id=7f4c1a
2026-03-19T22:14:02Z scim-handler WARN Falling back to legacy-parse -> created user payload but roles empty
```
Maria G: That "got" context looks like an old config string. Maybe the onprem installer/secret-import used the previous context value. Did we rotate and re-encrypt secrets with a different name?
Alex W: Ops rotated KMS alias last night using infra-runbooks script. We re-encrypted the scim webhook secret but maybe used default context. I can repro with the deployer's secret.
idp-admin: deploy-bot detected secret-rotation event for alias projects/redwood/kms/scim-key at 2026-03-19T21:58:10Z
Priya S: If decrypt fails with context mismatch, our code currently returns an empty roles set and we log a WARN. That would explain role-less accounts. But how did some users get admin instead of engineer?
Samir K: Two possibilities: 1) SCIM payload partial parse due to fallback picks wrong default role, 2) replayed old cached payload mapping in Redis that had stale role mapping. Any related cache errors?
Alex W: Yes, noticed redis WARN around same time: "cache: lookup miss -> fetching fallback-profile -> profile=admin-default"
Priya S: So sequence is: KMS decrypt fails -> fallback payload parse -> no roles -> role resolution service consults cache -> cache miss returns older default admin profile. Bad.
Maria G: Steps to mitigate: 1) stop automatic fallback to old profile when KMS decrypt fails (fail safe instead), 2) re-run re-encrypt with the correct context string and rotate secrets across onprem nodes, 3) issue an audit + fix script to reconcile affected users.
Alex W: For repro I ran this local curl to hit SCIM with the deployer token:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -X POST https://private-redwood.customer/scim/Users \n  -d '{"externalId":"u-999","userName":"test.user+scim@example.com"}'
```
And the log showed the context mismatch.
Samir K: Quick detection query for audit logs: 
```
SELECT timestamp, tenant_id, event, outcome FROM audit_logs 
WHERE event = 'scim.create' AND timestamp >= '2026-03-19' AND (meta->>'roles') IS NULL;
```
Maria G: Reconciliation plan (short):
- Pause SCIM consumer at ingress (customer can continue manual updates)
- Re-encrypt webhook secret using correct context: `kms-cli rewrap --alias=projects/redwood/kms/scim-key --context="scim-v1:org-123"`
- Deploy secret to all onprem nodes and clear small-role cache shard (shard-17)
- Run one-off job: `scripts/scim_reconcile --filter=tenant:org-123 --fix-roles` (idempotent)
Priya S: We should also add an alert in Console: count(scim.role_empty) > 5 in 10m -> pager. And add an audit rule to surface all KMS decrypt mismatches per tenant.
Alex W: Question — do we need to backfill audit entries with the KMS failure details? The onprem logs had the request_id but the central audit didn't ingest decrypt failure events previously.
Samir K: Yes, ingesting KMS failure events is useful. Quick patch: ship scim-handler's decrypt errors to audit topic with type=kms.decrypt_failed, include tenant_id and request_id. That helps triage without customer logs.
idp-admin: FYI idp team saw a handful of SAML assertion failures around the same rotation window for one tenant — clock skew + cert chain mismatch. Might be related to deploy timing.
Maria G: Also add a migration check: confirm SCIM secrets on disk include context label `scim-v1`. If any nodes have `scim:` fallback, fail fast during startup.
Alex W: I'll start the rewrap and push to canary nodes, then run reconcile on canary tenants. Will post results here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
